$comment: Scrapbook art data. Lengths are in units of a 400 x 400 artboard (multiply by artboard short side / 400), or given as percentages. Angles in degrees. Colours are roles only; hex values always come from the product's Wada combination. Numbers are rules of thumb drawn from the lineage in research.md unless a source is named.

line.$comment: The hand-drawn mark: marker or felt pen, used for one arrow, circle, underline or short note per piece.
line.continuity: One gesture per mark, drawn in a single stroke; an arrowhead may be a second stroke.
rules: Ink only (Wada Black, or the combination's ink role). Never the accent.
Every mark points at or frames the hero or the message.
No doodle fields, hearts or stars scattered for decoration.

shape.$comment: Pieces of paper and objects. Mostly rectangles, made human by how they are cut and placed.

torn.use: Newspaper strips behind words, notebook and grid paper, kraft paper.
torn.whiteCore: On coloured paper, show a 1-2 unit band of Wada White just outside the torn edge (the paper's core), as real coloured stock does when torn.
torn.sides: Tear one or two sides of a piece; at least one side stays straight so it still reads as a sheet.

cut.rule: Straight scissor edges, corners square or slightly clipped; may be 0.5-1 degree out of square.

dieCut.rule: Round, oval or rounded-rectangle with a white rim of 4-6% of the sticker's width.

rules: Every piece has a clear, recognisable silhouette: a photo looks like a photo, a ticket like a ticket.
Mix edge types: at least two of torn, cut and die-cut in one piece.
No perfect rows: no two neighbouring items share the same rotation.

corners.$comment: Corners for layout and UI around the collage (buttons, cards, image masks). Pixels at 1x for screens. Scrapbook UI uses paper-like near-square corners; stickers and tags are the round exceptions.

use.button: sm, styled as a label strip or a sticker (pill) for the primary action
use.card: xs, with a 1-2 degree rotation and a flat offset shadow
use.image: 0 inside a white border (instant photo), or torn edge

corners.print: Photos and tickets keep square or near-square corners; stickers are the only fully round items.

items.$comment: A headline made of several strips and letters counts as one item.

hero.rule: One hero, on the top layer of its area. Every other item is at most half its size.
hero.position: Centre or a third; never in a corner.

rotation.neverZero: At least 80% of items are rotated by 1 degree or more.

overlap.rule: Each item overlaps at least one neighbour. Overlaps never cover words, faces or the hero's focal point.

composition.readingPath: Headline (top 35%) -> hero -> message or subhead -> brand and call to action. Z-path or single column.

placements.use: Hero photo centred, headline strips top-left, supporting items around the lower edge. Posters, stories.
Two columns like an album page: hero on one side, notes and ticket on the other. Landscape banners, web heroes.
Items stacked toward one corner, the rest of the ground left clear for text. Square social posts.
One taped item and one handwritten note on a plain ground. Thumbnails, small banners, email headers.

composition.pairing: The ephemera tell the story the headline does not: a ticket stub says 'you were there', a stamp says 'sent', a label says 'kept'. Image and words add to each other.
rules: One focal point per piece: the hero.
Words sit on paper (a strip, a label, a note), never directly on busy collage.
Keep text strips at least one margin from the canvas edge; other items may bleed off at most two edges.

palette.$comment: Share of the visible area for each colour role. Colours come from the product's Wada combination.

ground.note: Kraft, cream, buff or newsprint grey work best.

paper.note: Photo borders, notes, strips, stickers' rims.

ink.from: Wada Black (or the combination's ink role)

accent.limit: At most two small items (e.g. one sticker and one ransom letter).

support.note: Tape, tickets, photo content, coloured paper scraps.

method: Start from a combination whose light-mode bg is a paper colour: cream, buff, ivory, kraft, pale yellow, pale pink or neutral grey (the album page).
Prefer combinations with inkUse 'body' so text on the ground passes AA; text on paper strips uses Wada Black.
Check there is one saturated colour for the accent (red, orange, pink, blue) and, if possible, one or two quieter support colours for tape and tickets.
Look at it as a zine: if the combination reads as photocopy, kraft and a stamp pad, it fits.

recommendedCombinations.why: Kraft paper, red stamp ink and black type: the classic zine and parcel palette.
Primary red, yellow and blue on a yellow ground: Dada and punk poster energy, ransom-note tiles.
Yellow ground with black type and a carmine accent: loud punk flyer, still AAA for text.
Newsprint grey with black and one red: photomontage and cut-up newspaper.
Aged album page with ballpoint blue and an orange sticker.
Victorian album: buff page, sienna and olive scraps, slate ink.
Kraft and card browns of Schwitters-style found paper; use where browns are positive (bread, coffee, craft).
Soft journaling page with a coral sticker and dark green pen.
Contemporary social collage: pink paper, lime tape, black type.
Cream page with a hot red ticket and grey newsprint scraps.

rules: No gradients, glows or blurred shadows. Flat offset shadows only (see texture.shadow).
Tape is the only translucent material (60-80% opacity).
Text colour on the ground uses the combination's text role (AA contrast); text on paper uses Wada Black.

shadow.rule: Same direction for every item in a piece. Tape and hand-drawn marks have no shadow.

tape.rotation: 30-50 degrees across a corner, or 0-15 degrees across an edge
tape.ends: Zigzag or slightly torn, 2-3 unit teeth
tape.colour: support colour (washi), the ground colour (kraft masking tape), or paper (matte tape)
tape.perItem: 1-2 pieces per taped item; at most 5 pieces per composition.

halftone.use: Printed matter: photos cut from magazines, newsprint, faded tickets.

paperGrain.specks: 100-160 ink specks of 0.4-1 unit at 8-12% opacity across the ground.
paperGrain.lined: Ruled or grid paper: lines every 10-12 units at 0.6 units, support or ink colour at 25-40% opacity.

stamp.ring: Double ring, outer stroke 2-2.5 units, with 2-3 small gaps (worn rubber).
stamp.rule: Stamps are never perfectly round in print: a gap or a light patch is required.

collage.$comment: Scrapbook-specific: how pieces are held and how much of each kind to use.
collage.fixingRule: Every item that is not a sticker or stamp shows at least one fixing, or is tucked under a neighbour.

vocabulary.$comment: Ephemera and what they usually say. Choose items from the product's own world, then pick the one that carries the message as the hero.

avoid.why: Unreadable, and reads as a threat in long form.
Generic decoration; says nothing about the product.

avoid.symbol: fake coffee rings, fake burn marks
avoid.why: Faked wear reads as costume, not memory.

avoid.symbol: real political figures, flags or protest imagery
avoid.why: Borrows a movement's meaning; easily misread or offensive (see research.md 5).

avoid.symbol: invented ticket numbers or dates presented as real
avoid.why: Misleading; use real event facts or obviously decorative ones.

method.$comment: How to build a collage that says one thing.
recipe: Write the one message in a sentence (W1).
List the things a customer would actually keep from the product: a receipt, a ticket, a photo, a label, a card.
Choose the hero: the one item that proves the message (a photo of the real moment, the ticket to the real event).
Add 2-4 supporting items that add facts the headline does not say (date, place, name, price).
Place headline and hero first, then supporting items along the reading path; tape them down; add one hand mark pointing to the hero or the message.
Remove one item. If nothing is lost, leave it out.

examples.hero: instant photo of the first loaf

examples.idea: a trip that belongs to you

checklist: One hero item, 30-45% of the canvas, on top.
4-7 items plus tape; 3-5 layers; every item rotated within -8 to +8 degrees (text strips within -2 to +2).
Each item overlaps a neighbour by 5-25%, and nothing covers words or the hero's focal point.
At least two edge types (torn, cut, die-cut); every item visibly fixed.
Flat offset shadows only, all in one direction; tape is the only translucent material.
Ransom-note type on one headline word at most; body on paper in the pairing's body face.
At least 25% of the ground visible; one combination, accent on two small items at most.
